about: Hand-maintained (Pass 6d Lane D, Pass 6c open findings 1, 2, 3 and 5; Pass 6d Lane N): behaviour gaps the release ships with. Each row names the inventory item (reference/inventory.json), the file whose code carries the gap (tools/deferred fails when it is missing), the reason, a reproduction, the generated docs pages whose "Known issues" section describes it (each must mention the id; the section comes from templates/resources/<name>.md.tmpl or templates/data-sources/<name>.md.tmpl) and whether CHANGELOG.md lists it under "Known issues" (it must then mention the id). Remove a row, its docs paragraph and its changelog bullet in the change that closes the gap. Read by tools/deferred into reference/_gen/deferred.json (kind known_issue).

issues.reason: driver = "cloud" (Docker Build Cloud) is tested only against a fake auth server and a fake BuildKit proxy (TestBuildxBuilderCloud, TestBKCloud*), never against the live service. Three behaviours follow buildx v0.38.2 by assumption: the provider dials the builder group at the default proxy build-cloud.docker.com:443 (buildx looks up per-platform instances through the Hub API), sends buildx-version: v0.38.2, and loads results through the build session (buildx's cloud pull is not implemented). The same gap is recorded as acceptance TestAccBuildxBuilderCloud_live (why the harness cannot run it), partial_marker buildx:builder and example resources/docker_buildx_builder (resource.docker_buildx_builder.cloud and output.cloud_builder); this row is the release note. Close all four when TestAccBuildxBuilderCloud_live has passed.

docker_compose (mode = "local") runs pre_start steps with per_replica: true once for every replica it creates and always removes a step container once it exits; compose v5.7.0 (pkg/compose/pre_start.go:115-147 runPreStart) rejects per_replica: true and keeps a failed step container for inspection. A project that uses per_replica applies with the provider but fails with docker compose up, and after a failed step there is no container left to inspect (the provider's error carries the last 20 log lines of the step).
issues.reproduce:
resource "docker_compose" "x" {
  name    = "prestart"
  content = <<-YAML
    services:
      web:
        image: nginx:alpine
        deploy: { replicas: 2 }
        pre_start:
          - command: ["sh", "-c", "exit 0"]
            per_replica: true
  YAML
}

terraform apply succeeds (two step containers run, both removed); docker compose -p prestart up -d with the same YAML fails.

issues.reason: docker_compose (mode = "local") applies use_api_socket: true by always adding the Engine socket bind mount, DOCKER_CONFIG=/run/secrets/docker (unless the service sets it) and the #apisocket config.json. compose v5.7.0 (apiSocket.go:45-132) adds DOCKER_CONFIG and the config file only when the host has registry credentials and the service does not set DOCKER_CONFIG, with mode 0600. In those two cases the com.docker.compose.config-hash label differs from the CLI's, so a container created by one is recreated by the other. Projects managed only by the provider are not affected.
issues.reproduce:
services:
  app:
    image: docker:cli
    command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
    use_api_socket: true
    environment: { DOCKER_CONFIG: /cfg }

docker compose -p apisock up -d with this file, then apply the same content with resource "docker_compose" "x" { name = "apisock" ... }: the plan recreates apisock-app-1 (the same happens with no DOCKER_CONFIG on a host with no registry credentials).

issues.reason: A compose project with a service build.ssh entry that has a path (id: path, e.g. default: /home/me/.ssh/id_ed25519) loses its whole structured project output on docker_compose and data.docker_compose_config: compose-go v2.16.2 SSHKey.MarshalJSON (types/ssh.go:49-54) writes "id": path, which is not valid JSON as a list element, so json.Marshal(types.Project) fails and composeProjectValue falls back to {"name": ...}. Every other field of project is null and no diagnostic is raised (the value never reaches the outputs contract). compose_yaml is not affected. Fix: marshal SSHKey entries in a fixup before encoding and make a failed encode a diagnostic.
issues.reproduce:
data "docker_compose_config" "x" {
  content = <<-YAML
    services:
      app:
        build:
          context: .
          ssh:
            default: /home/me/.ssh/id_ed25519
  YAML
}
output "svc" { value = data.docker_compose_config.x.project.services }

terraform apply: svc is null (project carries only name). The same content in docker_compose gives the same project.

issues.reason: data.docker_registry_image reads config, labels and created from the registry's image config blob with the provider's own registry client, because the daemon's GET /distribution/<name>/json returns no image config. That client falls back to plain HTTP only for localhost and loopback registries (as docker does), so for a plain-HTTP registry on any other host (a daemon insecure-registries entry served over http) the daemon path gives the warning 'Image config not read from registry' and leaves the three values null; digest, platforms and the raw output are still filled. insecure_skip_verify does not help there: it turns TLS verification off but still speaks HTTPS.
